video.title: Start This Simple Side Hustle Before Everyone Else Does

summary: Chris Koerner ranks five mobile/low-footprint sauna and cold plunge businesses in the US, from Denver Mobile Sauna (5th) to Purely Nomadic Sauna (1st). He pitches the sector as fast-growing, with claimed $10-50k/month operators and around 50% margins. Common themes are Facebook ads or Marketplace for leads, partnering with gyms and studios, tiered pricing, and a free first session. The last third is an interview with Danny of Purely Nomadic Sauna in Michigan, who is only 3-4 months in and has no revenue figures yet. The numbers are mostly second-hand and unverified.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; researched the industry and conducted the interview

speakers.name: Danny
speakers.description: Owner of Purely Nomadic Sauna, Grand Rapids, Michigan; also runs a home inspection business

ideas.name: Denver Mobile Sauna (mobile sauna and cold plunge rental)
ideas.one_liner: Drop-off rental of mobile sauna and cold plunge units, plus pop-up events with wellness studios.
ideas.business_model: Per-rental fees by duration, plus event partnerships
ideas.customer: Consumers and groups around Denver booking for private use; wellness studios for pop-ups
ideas.problem: People want sauna and cold plunge experiences without owning equipment
ideas.offer: Delivered mobile sauna and cold plunge units rented for hours, overnight or the weekend

pricing.model: Tiered by duration with a weekend upsell
pricing.notes: Host says price anchoring pushes about 70% of renters to the weekend option (unsourced).

acquisition_channels.details: Pop-up events with wellness studios give recurring revenue without a physical site.
Website bookings; the host implies customers arrive at the site intending to book hourly.

ideas.delivery: Owner drives units to the customer, drops off, maintains the equipment and collects it afterwards.

acquisition.how: Website SEO and ads could be run mostly by agents; studio partnerships need human outreach.

onboarding.how: Online booking and waiver flow is software-driven.

delivery.how: Physical towing, drop-off, set-up and pick-up every time.

support.how: Customer questions and issues mostly need a human or an agent with a human on call.

uk_applicability.notes: Mobile sauna hire works in the UK. Check insurance, towing licence limits and venue permissions. Prices will differ.

risks: Competition is high per the host

quotes.text: Here's how their pricing works. 300 bucks for 2 hours, 450 bucks for 4 hours, $5.25 for 8, or $600 for an overnight rental.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: If you do two to three rentals on the weekends, then you're making an extra $1 to $2,000 a month just from weekends.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Cedar Grove Sauna (Maine)
ideas.one_liner: Wood-fired sauna business with two fixed sites and a rotating mobile unit, built around community and authenticity.
ideas.business_model: Per-session sauna access at fixed locations plus mobile events
ideas.customer: Sauna enthusiasts and general public in Maine and New England
ideas.problem: Demand for an authentic sauna experience
ideas.offer: Public sauna sessions at two fixed locations plus a mobile unit that rotates weekly across New England

acquisition_channels.details: Email list of sauna aficionados who plan around the mobile unit's events.
Positioning as the local sauna expert, including study trips to Finland, Lithuania, Latvia and Sweden.

ideas.delivery: Staffed fixed locations plus a mobile unit; 8 staff.
unit_economics_claims: 10 cords of wood per year costing $400-900 each

acquisition.how: Email list and content marketing can be largely automated.

delivery.how: Staffed physical venues and wood-fired saunas.

uk_applicability.notes: Sauna culture and wood-fired saunas work in the UK. Planning permission and fire/safety rules apply for fixed sites.

risks: 8 staff and two sites need real operations management

quotes.text: she's serving 8 to 12,000 people per year.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: She only burns through 10 cords of wood annually.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Chill Wagon Wellness (Arizona)
ideas.one_liner: Trailer with cold plunges and sauna used for private bookings, festival events, corporate jobs and a branded 'plunge' event.
ideas.business_model: Private bookings, per-person event sessions, corporate flat fees
ideas.customer: Consumers in Phoenix/Scottsdale, gyms (Burn Boot Camp and others), festivals, corporate clients
ideas.problem: Wellness-minded people want recovery experiences; gyms and companies want attractive events
ideas.offer: Custom trailer (two cold plunges with jets, sauna for five, compression boots, synthetic turf) and a branded event: workout, cold plunge, sauna, coffee social

pricing.notes: Operational cost per event $30-60 (ice and gas).

acquisition_channels.details: Spent $3,500 on Facebook ads; claimed 80% of leads came from them.

quote.text: they spent 3,500 bucks on Facebook ads and generated 80% of leads from that ad spend
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Co-marketing with Burn Boot Camp and other local gyms; corporate and festival events.
Collect testimonials and case studies from partner business owners over consumer reviews.

ideas.delivery: Two founders run events with the trailer.

acquisition.how: Paid ads can be agent-run; B2B partnership calls need humans.

onboarding.how: Online booking, but event coordination is manual.

uk_applicability.notes: The model transfers, but the UK has far less year-round heat for plunge demand. Gym and corporate wellness partnerships exist in London.

risks: Added mobile IV therapy likely has regulatory risk

quotes.text: Vincent and Brock down in Arizona, 22 years old, doing over $60,000 in monthly revenue.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: charge $1,500 for a half day where all of the employees can use the units for free
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Drip Sauna (contrast therapy inside a gym, Texas)
ideas.one_liner: Infrared sauna and cold plunge room placed inside an existing gym, sold on a $75/month membership.
ideas.customer: Gym members and walk-ins in Cleburne, Texas
ideas.problem: Contrast therapy elsewhere requires a separate trip and costs $150-175/month
ideas.offer: Unlimited 45-minute sessions at under half the competitor price, inside the gym

acquisition_channels.details: Gym foot traffic and the gym's shared email list; the space sits on the route through the gym.
Facebook ads bring almost all customers for the stock tank installs.
Free first session and public/private plunges for viral sharing.

ideas.delivery: Four infrared saunas ($7-8k each, financeable) and two cold plunges ($10k each) in about two bedrooms of rented gym space at $2,000/month.
unit_economics_claims: Broke even in under a year including equipment
ideas.startup_cost: About $50-60k equipment (4 saunas at $7-8k plus 2 plunges at $10k) plus $2k/month rent
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Within a few months they had 130 members (after 2 years looking for a site)

acquisition.how: Gym partnership gives built-in traffic; ads can be agent-run.

onboarding.how: Membership signup and access can be software-run.

delivery.how: Equipment self-serve for members, but cleaning, water changes and maintenance need humans.

support.how: Members' queries can be handled by agents.

uk_applicability.notes: Gym-based contrast therapy works in the UK; UK gyms and studios are open to such tie-ins. Check business rates, water and electrical safety.

quotes.text: Within a few months, they had 130 monthly recurring members that were paying them $75 a month for unlimited usage of their units.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: they broke even in under a year, including paying off all their equipment
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: He bought two Colt plunges at $10,000 each. And he paid $2,000 a month to the gym to rent the space.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Purely Nomadic Sauna (Grand Rapids, Michigan)
ideas.one_liner: Side-business renting wood-burning mobile saunas by the day, weekend or week, with cold plunge add-ons, found via Facebook Marketplace.
ideas.business_model: Per-rental fees by day, weekend or week, plus add-on
ideas.customer: Health-and-wellness people, wedding parties, birthday parties, people trying a sauna before building one
ideas.problem: People want an authentic sauna experience without buying or building one
ideas.offer: Wood-burning mobile sauna delivered, with wood supplied and a how-to demo, then collected

pricing.notes: Priced off two competitors whose booking calendars he watched. Cold plunge is a paid add-on.

acquisition_channels.details: Free organic Facebook Marketplace listing with the day price in the title, weekend pricing in the description, and a link to the website.

quote.text: He finds his customers on Facebook Marketplace. That's it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Set up Google Business Profile, reviews, photos and website early to build a foundation.
Planned: Airbnbs and short-term rentals as an add-on, for off-season bookings.

ideas.delivery: Owner tows a 3,500 lb unit (needs a full-size truck) or a light aluminium/cedar unit, drops it off with wood, teaches use, then collects it.
unit_economics_claims: Insurance a couple thousand dollars per year
ideas.startup_cost: About $22,000 for the first unit, plus about $10,000 for the second; inflatable plunges a few hundred dollars; chillers $1,000-2,000
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Within the first weeks via Marketplace; first rentals before he was 4 months in

acquisition.how: Marketplace posting and Google profile can be agent-managed, though Marketplace automation may breach platform terms.

delivery.how: Towing, drop-off, demo, wood supply and pick-up are manual each time.

billing.how: Online payment through the booking tool.

uk_applicability.notes: UK has a growing mobile sauna hire market. Towing limits for a car licence, insurance, public-site permission and wood supply need checking. Inflatable plunges are easy to get.

risks: Strong seasonality; summer demand is weak
Early stage: no booking or revenue figures given

ideas.name: Stock tank cold plunge installation (Drip Sauna side business)
ideas.one_liner: Install stock-tank pools or plunges at customers' homes using Tractor Supply tanks and Amazon pool equipment.
ideas.problem: Residents want a cheap way to cool off at home
ideas.offer: Installed stock tank pool with grading and pool equipment
ideas.delivery: Buy tank and equipment, grade the land, install on site.

onboarding.how: Quote and booking can be digital.

support.how: Warranty and site issues need people.

uk_applicability.notes: Depends on a hot climate; the UK market for outdoor plunges is much shorter-season. Tractor Supply is US-only.

quotes.text: He makes around $1,500 profit per job on those stock tank installations.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Mobile IV therapy add-on
ideas.one_liner: Chill Wagon added mobile IV therapy as another revenue stream.

tactics.name: Price anchoring with a weekend upsell
steps: Offer hourly, overnight and weekend rates.
Set the weekend rate only slightly above the short-rental rate.
Delivery effort is the same for 2 hours or 2 days, so the longer rental adds margin.

quote.text: you might as well juice a little more revenue out of it
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Piggyback on an existing business's customer base
steps: Find a gym or wellness studio with unused space.
Negotiate rent and cross-promotion, such as an email list share.
Position the unit on the route through the gym so foot traffic is the marketing.

quote.text: He's got a built-in customer base on day one.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Free first session
steps: Give the first session free.
Convert to $75/month membership or $30 walk-ins.

quote.text: He makes this first session free. This creates an addiction.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Price off local competitors' calendars
steps: Watch competitors' booking calendars through the previous season.
Estimate how many weekends out they are booked.
Set similar prices.

tactics.name: Facebook Marketplace funnel
steps: Post the unit with day price in title.
Put weekend pricing and a website link in the description.
Website uses Squarespace with Acuity scheduling for booking.
If it works, boost the post, then move to proper Facebook ads.

tactics.name: Check local competition before entering
steps: Search Google Maps for competitors within an hour.
Use an ad scraper to see competitors' ads.
Either many competitors (market awareness) or none (first mover) can work.

tactics.name: Build Google presence early
steps: Set up Google Business Profile.
Collect reviews and photos.
Launch the website in the first couple of weeks.

tactics.name: Stack services and branded events
steps: Create a branded event (workout, plunge, sauna, coffee).
Co-market with gyms.
Add services to raise revenue per customer.

tactics.name: Counter seasonality
steps: Pair a seasonal business with one for the other season.
Partner with Airbnbs and lake rentals for off-season add-ons.

warnings.warning: Not installing drains under cold plunges makes water changes painful.

quote.text: Their one regret, they didn't install drains underneath the cold plunges because swapping out the water is kind of a pain.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Don't let customers use their own wood, since you can't control what they burn.

quote.text: is don't let people use their own wood.
quote.speaker: Danny

warnings.warning: Inflatable cold plunges are hard to keep cold in summer without a chiller.

quote.text: unless you have a chiller in the summertime in Michigan, it's hard to keep that water cold.
quote.speaker: Danny

warnings.warning: Summer demand for saunas is weak; a Minnesota operator couldn't generate enough bookings in the first two years.
The industry is still in the education phase, so patience is needed.
Danny would start with the lighter, cheaper unit because it is easier to tow.

lessons.lesson: Location, physical or digital, is the marketing; piggybacking on existing foot traffic cuts acquisition cost.

quote.text: Your location is your marketing.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Stack complementary services and events to raise revenue per customer.

quote.text: the money comes from stacking services to maximize your RPC, revenue per customer
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Community and expertise differentiate a commodity rental.

quote.text: community beats competition every single time
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Tiered pricing nudges buyers to larger packages.
Offset recurring revenue with high-ticket one-offs to smooth lumpy income.
Start small, test with a free Marketplace post, then scale ads as demand proves out.
Harder tasks like partnerships and events create differentiation.

quote.text: the harder way is usually the better way
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Buy lighter equipment first for easier logistics.
Either competitors or none can be a good signal; competition shows awareness, none lets you be first.
Local presence signals permanence and allows higher prices.
A genuine user of the product sustains a side business longer.

evidence_quality.rationale: Mostly second-hand profiles with unverified claims (operators' revenue, margins, search growth). The Danny interview is first-hand but he is only 3-4 months in and gives no revenue data. The Drip Sauna figures come from an earlier interview.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host promotes Go High Level via affiliate link, his TK Owners community, a Facebook Ads guide and his newsletter.
